content: Ligand 2 is a small chloro-methylquinoline with QED 0.602; ligand 1 is a 445 Da hydantoin toluidide with a bromoaryl, QED 0.752, and both are completely inactive. Neither has anything to contribute by crossover. Ligand 1 does have a terminal aryl methyl at atom 0 over an acyclic bond, so anchoring there keeps that single carbon and discards the other 26 atoms. This episode finishes the acyl-cap ring-size series: an acetyl cap measured 0.15, a propanamide 0.12, a cyclopropanecarboxamide 0.25, and I am testing cyclobutane elsewhere this generation - so cyclopentane brackets it from above and tells me whether the cap effect is about ring strain and rigidity or simply about bulk. I attach through a pyridine C4 so the surviving methyl becomes the 4-methyl, with the fragment supplying the anilide and the cyclopentyl. Expected product: N-{4-[(4-methylpyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopentanecarboxamide at about 295 Da.
